newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Nine police wounded in riots in French Guiana.
newsitem.headline: Nine police wounded in riots in French Guiana.

text.p: Nine police were wounded during a night of ferocious riots in French Guiana ignited by the detention of three members of the territory's independence movement, officials said on Thursday.
French government officials said that eight of the nine injured police were hit by gunfire in the second consecutive night of violence in the capital Cayenne.
Officials also said three shops were sacked as armed rioters and police clashed until four a.m. on Thursday (0700 GMT). The sound of gunfire and tear gas grenade explosions had started as night fell.
The riots were triggered after police arrested Jean-Victor Castor and Fabien Canavy, both members of the Guiana Workers Union (UTG) which favours independence from France.
Jean-Claude Ringuet, a member of the pro-independence Guiana National Popular Party (PNPG), gave himself up to police after taking refuge for several hours in Cayenne's town hall on Tuesday.
Police cordoned off the city's main boulevard in front of the central police station, where the three are being held.
Lawyers for the three said police were planning to transfer them to the French Caribbean island of Martinique. Supporters of the three have vowed to prevent the transfer.

French officials pledged last week to crack down on violence in its South American overseas territory after a new wave of violence last week in which two police were wounded and several shops ransacked.
They said more than 150 police reinforcements have been flown in from France since the weekend.

Unrest this month followed arrests including that of Alain Michel, a founding member of the PNPG. Michel was detained on April 11 and taken the next day with four others to Martinique aboard a military aircraft.

He was charged with arson and violence against a magistrate when the residence of French Guiana's state prosecutor was attacked last November. In that wave of riots, one person was killed and millions of dollars worth of property was damaged.
Michel faces up to 20 years in prison if convicted, his lawyer said.

French Guiana, on the northeast coast of South America, is the only non-independent territory on the Western Hemisphere mainland. Its economy is heavily dependent on subsidies from France and 23 percent of the population of 150,000 is unemployed.
